We completed the owner-approved feedback label collection for MAST-U remediation.
The collection uses training equilibria and excludes both test equilibria. The
surrogate, guard and closed-loop acceptance limit remain unchanged.

We reviewed the finished local artifacts before considering training. The review
checks the allocation against the approved resource and time limits, verifies
checksums and provenance, and compares every label input row with its selected
case and source trajectory. It also checks the case budget, unique coordinates,
training-only equilibrium selection, source-model identity and finite successful
labels: [eight local checks pass for approved allocation/time, hashes and lineage, full-input alignment, case budget, unique coordinates, training-only equilibria, source model and finite successful labels]{.claim}[C-183](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-183){.cid .st-measured}.

| stage | result |
|---|---|
| completed collection | [eight local checks pass for approved allocation/time, hashes and lineage, full-input alignment, case budget, unique coordinates, training-only equilibria, source model and finite successful labels]{.claim}[C-183](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-183){.cid .st-measured} |
| artifact synchronization | awaiting explicit approval |
| training and coupled revalidation | pending |

The new evidence establishes that the collected labels retain their full solver
inputs and their source lineage. It does not establish held-out model accuracy or
an improved temperature trajectory. The existing failed MAST-U acceptance result
remains open ([K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030)).

**What's next.** Synchronize the reviewed artifacts after approval, then prepare
training and validation while preserving the test split and the owner-required
monotonicity constraint. Another coupled comparison must assess the unchanged
closed-loop limit before any claim of successful remediation.
